decision: Launch with one series: 'Sky This Week' — weekly, location-specific, computed night-sky guide (vertical short, 40–55 s)
rationale: Best fit of (a) defensible quality: every claim is computed from ephemerides, so we can't drift into slop, (b) recurring demand with natural weekly novelty, (c) monetisation beyond Shorts ads (gear/sponsor fit: Astronomy.com's weekly sky column is Celestron-sponsored), (d) low risk under YouTube's July-2026 'inauthentic content' clarification, which targets repetitive mass-produced content rather than AI-assisted work with original input. Shorts RPM is small for any niche (estimates /usr/bin/zsh.04–1.44 for education), so Shorts are treated as a funnel; long-form and sponsors are the revenue path. Review after 8 published episodes using recorded metrics.
alternatives: General space-facts shorts (rejected: most saturated slop niche, no data moat)
Science/tech news shorts (deferred: needs sourced-facts workflow + speed; good second series once the pipeline is proven)
Long-form explainers first (deferred: higher RPM but far more production per video; reuse templates later)

decision: Imagery policy: real data and real images only (computed sky, NASA/ESA public imagery with credits); AI-generated images off by default, allowed only when labelled and recorded with aiGenerated=true
rationale: User preference; also the channel's whole differentiation is accuracy. AI images of real objects would undermine the 'computed, not made up' promise.

decision: Human approval gate stays on (autoApprove=false); synthetic voice is disclosed on every platform (TikTok video_made_with_ai, description line)
rationale: A wrong date or direction destroys trust in a 'where to look' channel; the gate costs ~5 min/week. Disclosure is honest and avoids policy risk.

decision: Switch package manager from npm to pnpm 12 (packageManager pinned); allow native builds only for esbuild, onnxruntime-node, sharp; deny protobufjs postinstall
rationale: User asked. Strict resolution prevents phantom dependencies, faster installs/CI, pnpm's minimum-release-age gives a supply-chain buffer. Verified: typecheck, lint, 73 tests, Remotion bundle, Kokoro TTS and a Remotion still render all work under pnpm.
alternatives: Stay on npm (works, but looser resolution)
bun (faster, but less mature with Remotion/onnxruntime)

decision: Self-host Postiz from this repo (infra/postiz): official compose adapted with secrets in a gitignored .env, pinned images (postiz-app v2.25.3), ports on 127.0.0.1, Renovate PRs for the stack never automerged
rationale: User requirement (self-hosted, operated by Claude). Pinned tags + Renovate keep it current without surprise upgrades; Temporal/Elasticsearch versions follow upstream postiz-docker-compose for compatibility.

decision: Dependencies on latest versions; exception: TypeScript held at 6.0.x
rationale: typescript-eslint 8.72 (latest) declares peer typescript <6.1.0; TypeScript 7 would break linting. Encoded in renovate.json allowedVersions so it lifts deliberately.

decision: Channel brand: 'Photon Sphere', handle @thephotonsphere on YouTube and TikTok; separate identity (Proton mail thephotonsphere@proton.me + dedicated Google account), not the owner's personal accounts. 'Sky This Week' stays a series inside the channel.
rationale: Owner chose the name (black-hole photon ring = light, fits a channel about what light shows us; black-hole logo). YouTube channel search 2026-11-11/12: 'Event Horizon' is crowded (John Michael Godier's verified 335k channel @EventHorizonShow with a black-hole logo, plus 6+ others), 'Parallax' crowded (7+ incl. verified Parallax Science); 'Photon Sphere' only has tiny users (@photon-sphere ~81 subs, a ~500-sub music artist). Bare @photonsphere was taken on Proton/YouTube, so the 'the' prefix is used everywhere for consistency.
alternatives: Event Horizon (crowded, confusable with a larger channel)
Naked Eye / Light Lag / Umbra (not chosen)

decision: Platforms at launch: YouTube Shorts + TikTok. Meta (Instagram/Facebook) skipped for now. First episodes uploaded manually; Postiz automation after the channel is warmed up. No phone number on the new accounts.
rationale: Owner does not want to link a phone or personal Facebook profile; Meta requires a real personal profile to own a Page. Manual uploads first avoid API-posting new accounts (unaudited YouTube/TikTok API apps post private-only anyway).
alternatives: Create Page under owner's personal Facebook
Automate via Postiz from day one

decision: Channel logo and banner: procedural black hole (shadow, photon ring, lensed accretion disk) rendered by Remotion stills 'Logo' and 'Banner' (video/brand/), output in brand/. Uploaded to YouTube and TikTok profiles.
rationale: Owner wanted a black-hole logo; drawn in code from our own renderer (no AI imagery, rule 5), reproducible with 'pnpm exec remotion still video/index.tsx Logo brand/logo.png'. Banner text kept inside YouTube's 1546x423 all-device safe area.
alternatives: NASA/EHT M87* image (licensing + would look like a news channel)

decision: Publishing provider switched from self-hosted Postiz to Buffer (free plan, 3 channels: YouTube + TikTok). Postiz client, infra/postiz stack, operate-postiz skill, CI job and Renovate rules removed (kept in git history). Videos are hosted as release assets of a public GitHub repo because Buffer's API only accepts media by URL.
rationale: With our own Postiz OAuth apps, YouTube and TikTok keep API uploads private until app audits pass (weeks), and TikTok also needs a public HTTPS domain + verified media domain. Buffer's apps are already audited, so posts are public immediately; no domain, no laptop-must-be-on scheduling, no 6-container upkeep. Buffer's GraphQL API (GA July 2026) supports scheduled video posts with YouTube (title, privacy, category, isAiGenerated) and TikTok (isAiGenerated) metadata — verified by schema introspection on 2026-11-12.
alternatives: Keep Postiz + Cloudflare tunnel/domain + platform audits
Postiz for some platforms, Buffer for others

decision: Repository made public; approved videos are hosted as release assets of this repo (publishing.mediaHost.repo = Nasus20202/ContentCreator) for Buffer to fetch.
rationale: Owner accepted that the public repo links the channel to their GitHub identity; in exchange: zero extra accounts, direct download URLs, and the fact-check/decision trail is publicly verifiable (fits the 'computed, not guessed' brand). History scanned for secrets before publishing: none (only placeholders; .env files gitignored).

decision: Repository made public. Approved videos are committed to the orphan 'videos' branch of this repo and served from raw.githubusercontent.com for Buffer to fetch (publishing.mediaHost: git-branch).
rationale: Owner accepted that the public repo links the channel to their GitHub identity; in exchange: no extra accounts, direct download URLs, and the fact-check/decision trail is publicly verifiable. Owner preferred a branch over release assets. History scanned for secrets before going public: none (placeholders only; .env files gitignored).
